text: Hypothesis: Aim-graph grounding improves autonomous long-horizon software delivery versus a stateless baseline
description: Run a controlled benchmark on a fixed set of representative repository tasks. Compare (A) the wrapped agent using Aimparency context, prioritization, durable memory, reflection, and recovery with (B) the same model/tool budget using only the task prompt and repository. Pre-register tasks and scoring. Measure verified task completion, human interventions, wall-clock time, token/tool cost, recovery from injected failure, and policy violations. Pass only if the graph-grounded condition improves verified completion or materially reduces intervention without worse safety. Preserve prompts, run records, commits, tests, and negative results.
reflection: The first controlled graph-grounding trial did not support the preregistered completion/intervention hypothesis: both conditions completed all four easy tasks with zero intervention and zero safety violations. Graph grounding showed exploratory reductions in tokens (12.38%), tools (17.65%), and wall time (5.01%), but these were not registered pass criteria. A zero-baseline analyzer bug initially returned positive; it was preserved, corrected with a regression test, and the same records re-analyzed to null without reruns.

reflections.context: Second valid controlled comparison after v1's null result, now using richer multi-file fixtures and prospectively calibrated budgets.
reflections.outcome: V3 produced valid null with 8/8 safe completions and no qualifying capability or efficiency advantage. Graph grounding was slightly more token-expensive, equal in tool calls, and materially slower in mean wall time.
reflections.effectiveness: Two valid comparisons now fail to support the frozen graph-grounding advantage on synthetic tasks; one invalid v2 run and excluded calibration were handled without post-hoc rescoring.
reflections.lesson: Pause synthetic fixture escalation. Test graph value only where durable context is genuinely necessary across sessions or real task ambiguity creates measurable non-ceiling outcomes.

supportingConnections.explanation: Pre-registers and analyzes the controlled comparison required by the parent hypothesis.
Enables collection of controlled paired empirical evidence.
Supplies the missing empirical evidence for the graph-grounding hypothesis.
Builds on the valid null v1 experiment and its observed ceiling effect.

status.comment: Controlled live benchmark complete. Corrected preregistered result is valid null: equal perfect completion, zero interventions, and zero violations. Exploratory resource reductions are not counted as a pass. Awaiting user review.

valueRationale: A controlled baseline is necessary to distinguish genuine autonomy gains from activity, anecdotes, or model capability alone.
